headline: Triangle all warm side; the break sits on blown-out Santa Rosa
body:
Small craft advisory everywhere this morning: the channel and Anacapa zones through this evening, the outer waters and the Santa Rosa zone through late Tuesday night. Expect NW 25 to 30 kt and 7 to 9 ft out west today, and a southerly swell running through Tuesday from two tropical systems well offshore.

Monday is the day, and it's a dawn deal. The triangle middle has 8 to 10 kn NW early over 5.7 ft, then it falls apart — 13 kn by noon, 25 kn WNW gusting 29 by three. Tuesday starts harder, 15 kn g18 at six, and ends worse, 24 g30.

Placement is the problem. All three corners are warm: west 70, south 72.5, east 73. The 64–68 band is not inside the zone. Start on the west corner south of Santa Cruz, the coolest water and the edge the break lies beyond, and work bait.

The actual break is Santa Rosa Flats at 67.5, but it's 7.7 ft and 21 to 29 kn NW both days. Don't make that run. Osborn and San Nicolas are 72 to 73 — no break, not worth 68 or 73 miles.
